title: Complementing bounded-error decisions
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, $L$ a language of binary strings, and $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ a space bound. If $N$ uses at most $s(|x|)$ work-tape cells on every input and every choice word, and for each input $x$ there is a time bound at which all branches halt and the probability of outputting the one-bit membership value for $L$ is at least $2/3$, then the machine obtained by complementing every bit it outputs has the same space bound and decides the complement of $L$ with the same probability threshold and halting guarantee.
